seo.title: Budget Plan for Rs 30k–150k Salary in Pakistan (2026)
seo.description: Ready-made monthly budgets for a Rs 30,000, 50,000, 75,000, 100,000 or 150,000 salary in Pakistan, for one person or a family of four, rupee by rupee.

h1: Monthly budget plan for any salary in Pakistan
summary: Sample monthly budgets for Rs 30,000, 50,000, 75,000, 100,000 and 150,000 take-home pay, for a single person and a family of four, and how to adapt them to your own life.
intro_html:
Whether you earn Rs 30,000 or Rs 1,50,000 a month, the question is the same: how much should go on rent, food, bills and school fees, and how much can you save? A plan written down before payday works far better than checking what is left at the end of the month.

This guide gives a sample budget for five take-home salaries, for a single person and for a family of four. They are examples, not averages: your rent, city and family will change the numbers. Use them as a starting point, then put your own figures into the calculator.

sections.h2: Monthly budget plans at a glance
sections.body_html:
The table shows how much each sample plan saves, or puts into a committee or emergency fund, every month. All amounts are monthly take-home pay, after tax and deductions.

Take-home paySingle person: savingsFamily of 4: savings
Rs 30,000Rs 3,000 (10%)Rs 1,500 (5%)
Rs 50,000Rs 8,000 (16%)Rs 1,000 (2%)
Rs 75,000Rs 18,000 (24%)Rs 4,000 (5%)
Rs 1,00,000Rs 30,000 (30%)Rs 6,000 (6%)
Rs 1,50,000Rs 55,000 (37%)Rs 15,000 (10%)

These are example plans written for this guide, not survey results. For comparison, the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics' Household Integrated Economic Survey (HIES) 2024-25 found that the average household spent Rs 79,150 a month, and that 36.72% of spending went on food and 25.72% on housing, water, electricity and gas. The average household had 5.98 members.

A family of four on a lower salary has very little room to save. That is normal, not a failure. Even Rs 1,000 a month builds the habit.

sections.h2: How to build your own monthly budget plan
sections.body_html:
1. Start with take-home pay. Use the amount that actually reaches your account, not your gross salary.
  2. List the fixed costs. Rent, school fees, a committee payment, loan instalments and the internet package. These are paid first.
  3. Estimate the bills that change. Use last year's electricity and gas bills, not just last month's. Summer bills are much higher.
  4. Set a food budget. Monthly rashan plus weekly vegetables, milk and meat. Our family grocery budget guide shows how to set one you can keep.
  5. Pay yourself on payday. Move your savings amount out of your main account the day the salary arrives, before anything else.
  6. Keep a small "other" line. Shaadi gifts, a doctor's visit or a broken phone screen always turn up. A budget with no room for them breaks in the first week.

If you prefer a simple rule, the 50/30/20 rule splits pay into needs, wants and savings. On a low salary in a big city, needs often take far more than 50%, so treat it as a target, not a test.

sections.h2: Budget plan for Rs 30,000 a month
sections.body_html:

RentRs 9,000 (shared room)Rs 0 (family-owned home)
Electricity, gas and waterRs 3,000Rs 5,500
Food and groceriesRs 8,000Rs 14,000
TransportRs 3,000Rs 2,500
School fees and booksRs 0Rs 3,000
Mobile and internetRs 1,000Rs 1,000
Medicine and doctorRs 1,000Rs 1,500
Personal and otherRs 2,000Rs 1,000
Savings or committeeRs 3,000Rs 1,500

Rs 30,000 is below the federal minimum wage of Rs 40,700 a month for 2026-27, so a family of four can only manage on it without rent. The example assumes the family lives in a home it owns or shares with relatives, and children go to a low-fee or government school. Food takes nearly half of the pay.

At this level, the priority is a small cushion of one week's costs, so one surprise doesn't lead to borrowing.

A single person can save around 16% here, even with rent. For a family, the rent line decides almost everything: a portion in an older area or outside the city centre is what makes this plan work. Watch the electricity bill in summer, when it can easily double.

At this level, the biggest risk is lifestyle creep: ordering in more often, a bigger phone plan, a car instalment. If a car loan is tempting, add the instalment, petrol, insurance and maintenance to this table first and see what is left for savings.

With savings of Rs 15,000 to Rs 55,000 a month, the question becomes where to keep the money. Our guide to committees, bank savings and National Savings compares the options. For a big goal such as a wedding or Hajj, read how to save for a wedding, Hajj or Umrah.

sections.h2: Keep the plan working when prices rise
sections.body_html:
Prices in Pakistan can change fast. The Pakistan Bureau of Statistics reported consumer price inflation of 9.6% in October 2026 compared with a year earlier, and an average of 7.05% over 2025-26. A budget that worked last year may not work this year.

  • Review the plan twice a year, and after every rent increase, school fee notice or electricity tariff change.
  • Raise your savings when your pay rises. Put at least half of any increment into savings before you get used to spending it.
  • Keep savings growing faster than prices where you can. Money in a current account earns nothing while prices rise.
  • Compare with the average. Our guide to average monthly household expenses in Pakistan shows what households actually spend, category by category.

faq.q: How much should I save from a Rs 50,000 salary in Pakistan?
faq.a: In our example plans, a single person saves about Rs 8,000 a month (16%) and a family of four about Rs 1,000. The right amount depends on your rent and family size. Start with any fixed amount on payday and raise it when your pay rises.

faq.q: Can a family of four live on Rs 30,000 a month?
faq.a: Only with no rent and very careful spending. Rs 30,000 is below the federal minimum wage of Rs 40,700 a month for 2026-27. Our example assumes a family-owned home and low school fees, and food takes nearly half of the money.

faq.q: What is the average household spending in Pakistan?
faq.a: The Household Integrated Economic Survey 2024-25 by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics found average household consumption spending of Rs 79,150 a month: Rs 95,533 in urban areas and Rs 67,894 in rural areas.

faq.q: Should I count a committee as savings in my budget?
faq.a: Yes, a committee payment is money you get back, so it can sit on the savings line. But it earns no profit and carries a risk if a member stops paying, so keep an emergency fund in a bank or National Savings as well.

No. They are example plans written for this guide to show one realistic way to split each salary. Your rent, city, school fees and family size will change every line, so use the calculator with your own numbers.
